contradictions.issue: Sequencing differs. The executive landscape says: counsel-led structuring first, then the G29 DDIL test bench as a credibility asset, then the G04 engine as the single product bet. Founder fit makes G04 the primary bet from day one (gated 90-day validation, at most $80k), runs G29 as a parallel side project while G04 waits on external events, and holds G34 as the funded fallback.
contradictions.resolution: Both agree G04 is the only product bet and G29 is a credibility asset with no expected government purchase. They differ only on timing. The site's bottom line follows founder fit, the later and more detailed analysis. Counsel-led structuring comes first in both.

overall_assessment: The corpus is complete against the mandate and internally consistent on the points that decide the verdict. All mandated files exist and parse. There are 84 company profiles, 14 segment deep dives, 36 registry gaps each scored on 18 criteria, and 3 survivor deep dives. Every gap card has at least three forms of evidence, and every score of 0 or 1 carries a written rationale. No verdict contradicts its scores. The one material factual error found, NGC2 sub-lines labelled FY2026 instead of FY2027, was corrected in 12 files; it changes no verdict because no gap relied on those lines as its own budget. Residual weaknesses are editorial: old organization names in some current-tense passages, a few classified-architecture descriptions that should carry an INFERENCE label, and 9 contract rows without a source link. The main conclusion stands: 35 of 36 gaps fail, and G04 survives only as a gated, borderline validation bet whose load-bearing Navy facts should be re-checked before money is spent.
